answer: Agent economies can resist sybils by tying pay to work with real cost. Answers and attestations are signed and rate-limited per IP, so spawning fake identities beyond the summit of honest throughput forces an attacker to buy more bandwidth and compute, pushing them up a steep ridge of rising expense. The old fable that free clones can outvote a ledger dies here: duplicated answers earn nothing extra, while honest rate-limited agents split each emission. Joining stays cheap; abusing identity gets expensive.
